question: What did a 2008 analysis of the whole history of world records in athletics, swimming and cycling find about their progress?
answer: That it is slowing toward a ceiling. Berthelot and colleagues fitted every record since 1896 and found the curves flattening: new marks beat old ones by ever thinner margins. In their reading, the big human gains of the twentieth century were a brief burst; leaps now come mostly from equipment.
move: When each gain is smaller than the last, ask how near the ceiling is.
ask: Where am I expecting the same big gains as before, when I may be close to my own ceiling?
reference: Berthelot et al., The Citius End: World Records Progression Announces the Completion of a Brief Ultra-Physiological Quest, PLoS ONE, 2008
